newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel complains to France over de Charette visit.
newsitem.headline: Israel complains to France over de Charette visit.

text.p: Israel has lodged an official complaint with France for deciding to send Foreign Minister Herve de Charette on only a 24-hour visit to the Jewish state next week, an Israeli official said on Monday.
Israeli Foreign Ministry spokesman Ygal Palmor said the French ambassador was summoned last week to the ministry where "we expressed our discontent over changes in the programme for the visit".
Palmor said Paris had originally promised "a full state visit of two or three days".
On Friday, the French Foreign Ministry said de Charette would visit Israel, Lebanon and Syria from March 4-6.

"We don't mind what he does in the region once he is here but instead of dedicating two to three days to Israel on a full-scale visit, he will be here for a 24-hour visit which will include a visit to the Palestinian Authority," Palmor said.
"Since there had been a promise (of a longer visit), the minister instructed the ministry to express his discontent," he said, referring to Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy.

"We were supposed to discuss bilateral issues and the peace process but it was also supposed to a 'get-acquainted' visit with representatives of Israeli society not only with the prime minister and foreign minister," Palmor told Reuters.

Last week, the French Foreign Ministry expressed concern over Israeli plans to build new housing for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem, saying the project would end a "climate of confidence" following Israel's troop redeployment from Hebron.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has pledged to build 6,500 Jewish homes at Jabal Abu Ghneim or Har Homa, a hill of pine trees between Jerusalem and Bethlehem captured by Israel in the 1967 war.
